label: journal index
description: The first page of your journal, ruled by hand. A tab down the edge for each child you see. There is one so far, Wren, and under it a column of weeks, with a gap at the bottom where today will go.

label: Wren, intake form
description:
The intake form, clipped inside the front cover of your journal, filled in by two hands in two pens. Under what brought you here, Mom has written that Wren has been so good, honestly no trouble at all. Dad has written that she is a good little trooper.

Under changes in the family, both of them have ticked the box for separation.

label: Wren, school referral
description:
A letter on school letterhead, from Ms. Okafor, folded into the back pocket of your journal. She writes that Wren used to share news every morning and lately just says pass. At lunch Wren sorts the class library into piles by color.

She adds that Wren is kind to everyone and has never once been a problem.

label: Wren, November 7
description: Your own notes, in your small square writing. Wren stayed by the door for ten minutes, holding the rabbit by one ear. She lined her shoes up. She told you her name and the day of the week, and nothing else.

label: Wren, November 14
description:
Session two. Wren built a tower of blocks without a word, knocked it down, and put every block back in the bin. She counted under her breath, and then stopped herself.

Underlined in pencil. Did not name the move. W. left the table when I said "two houses."

label: Wren, family schedule
description:
A typed page, taped into your journal. Weekdays are at Mom's. Tuesday nights are at Dad's, and every second weekend. Thursday is a Mom day.

In the margin, in Dr. Bell's green ink. Both parents attentive. Child very tidy. Go slowly.

label: The Bird Who Carried Her Nest
aliases: the bird who carried her nest
description: A thin picture book. On the cover, a round brown bird holds a nest in both wings, with a tree on either side of her.

label: Bear Counts to Ten
description: A fat, cheerful picture book. On the cover, a bear holds one paw up, and ten red balloons float over his head.

label: Two Houses for Fox
description: A picture book with a fox standing between two small houses. A sticker on the spine reads Changing Families.

label: clementine and crackers
description: A clementine and four square crackers on a paper napkin.

label: Wren, November 21
description: Session three. Dad dropped her off on a Thursday, and that threw her off from the start. She sorted the animals into the two bins until both sides were even. The story did not land today, and she stayed with the things she could count.

label: Wren, November 21
description: Session three. W. showed me the notebook she keeps in Rabbit's bag, yellow squares for Mom and green for Dad, ticked every night before bed. Since the afternoon nobody came for her at school, she has been trying to keep the schedule straight on her own.

label: Wren, November 21
description: Session three. She showed me the handle. It was from one of Mom's blue cups, broken while she was trying to bring her tea, right before the first big fight she heard. She has been carrying it in Rabbit's bag since the spring because she thinks the cup is why they live in two houses now. I stayed with her and did not rush to talk her out of it.

label: Wren, her drawing
description: Wren's drawing, in crayon, pressed between two pages. A row of crayons, all the same length, colored in one at a time.

label: Wren, her drawing
description: Wren's drawing, in crayon, pressed between two pages. A small brown bird with a nest held in both wings, between two trees. Biscuit is drawn in the corner of the page.

label: Wren, her drawing
description: Wren's drawing, in crayon, pressed between two pages. A bird sitting on the ground between two trees, with no nest in her wings. Beside her, very small, a girl holds up a red stop sign.

label: journal index
description: The first page of your journal, ruled by hand. A tab down the edge for each child you see. Wren is under the first, with a column of weeks that ends in November. Leo is under the second, with a column of Tuesdays, and a gap at the bottom where today will go.

label: Leo, intake form
description:
The intake form, clipped inside the front cover of your journal, filled in by two hands in two pens. Under what brought you here, Claire has written that her father died in his sleep in December. They told Leo that Pop's body got very old and very tired, so he went to sleep. Since then Leo has come down the hall to their room two or three times a night, and he will not let her close her eyes on the couch after work.

Marcus has written underneath that Leo is full of energy, and has been playing hospital nonstop.

Under changes in the family, both of them have ticked the box for a death.

label: Leo, school referral
description:
A letter on school letterhead, from Ms. Chen, folded into the back pocket of your journal. She writes that Leo asked for a pass to the nurse four times in two weeks, with no fever and nothing hurt. Each time he only wanted the nurse to listen to his chest with the stethoscope and tell him the number.

She adds that whenever she picks up her coffee mug at her desk, he asks if she is getting too tired.

label: Leo, January 28
description:
Your own notes, in your small square writing. Leo opened every bin and drawer in the playroom to see what was inside. In the last five minutes he found the doctor's kit, and he told you that next Tuesday the playroom would be a clinic, and that you would need patients from the basket upstairs.

He said he is going to be an emergency room doctor, or the night watchman at the zoo, because somebody has to make sure the hippos don't roll over on each other.

label: Leo, family schedule
description:
A typed page, taped into your journal. Tuesdays at four. Claire drops him off and picks him up.

In the margin, in Dr. Bell's green ink. Seven is a literal age. Be careful with "sleep" and "tired."

label: The Little Owl Who Kept Watch
aliases: the little owl who kept watch
description: A thin picture book. On the cover, a small owl in an acorn helmet marches along a branch under a round moon.

label: Doctor Rabbit's Busy Clinic
description: A bright, busy picture book. On the cover, a rabbit in a white coat holds a clipboard, and a line of animals waits with bandaged paws.

label: The Long Sleep in the Clouds
aliases: the long sleep in the clouds
description: A soft gray picture book. On the cover, an old bear lies on a cloud under the moon. A sticker on the spine reads Losing Someone.

label: basket of stuffed animals
description: A wicker basket with a one-eyed frog, an owl and a lamb in it, all a little worn at the ears.

label: pretzel sticks and oat cookies
description: A handful of pretzel sticks and three oat cookies on a paper napkin.

label: Leo, February 4
description: Session two. Leo ran the playroom as a clinic and kept every stuffed animal propped upright against the wall. He stayed inside the doctor game the whole time. Next week, stay in the nurse role and let him set the rules.

label: Leo, February 4
description: Session two. Leo had me write the warning signs on the back of his chart. Lines by Owl's eyes, and three white hairs on Frog. He counted them himself. Keep giving him plain, literal answers next week.

label: Leo, February 4
description: Session two. He showed me the red squeeze light Pop gave him. Every night he stands outside his parents' door in the dark and squeezes it just long enough to see their blanket rise and fall. Before he left, he laid the one-eyed frog flat on the cloth to sleep. Next week, let him decide whether the clinic still needs a night watch.

label: Leo, his chart
description: Leo's chart, folded into your journal. A sheet of drawing paper with 24 BEATS across the top in red crayon.

label: Leo, his chart
description: Leo's chart, folded into your journal. In your handwriting, OWL, WRINKLES, and FROG, 3 WHITE HAIRS. Under them, in green crayon, one line. REGULAR TIRED.

label: Leo, his chart
description: Leo's chart, peeled off the table and folded into your journal. In red crayon, SLEEPING. CHEST GOES AUTOMATIC. WILL WAKE UP.
